why_this_direction: Step 5 is the correction made again on the model's own trace until the gap has closed. The first relational step was one step taken on a text held fixed under the tolerance at the members' mean: it read lower on that text (0.9411 of its start) and higher on the answers the stepped model writes itself in torch (2.6673 times). Marcos's diagnosis names what was wrong in how that step was applied, and the original's own derivative bears each part out (records/development/2026-11-15-relation-reading/grad-split-mean.json, grad-split-envelope.json; studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/relation-envelope-original/result.json): (1) correct paths were given gradient: 0.368 of that step's first-order gain lay on the fifteen correct answers, pointing the same way as the wrong answers' part (cosine 0.8), and a position was inside the tolerance at all 105 merges at only 2664 of 19751 positions; (2) under the successes' envelope no correct cell is over its tolerance on the original and the fifteen wrong answers hold all of the loss, 0.0527 over 138187 cells; (3) the torch forward's own distance from the engine's states would by itself put 0.156 of the gradient's gain back on correct answers at the envelope's edge, which the anchor of the forward on the engine's distances removes; (4) only one step was ever taken: the specification's loop (a step, the answers written again, the trace read again, the next step from the state reached, whatever was read) has not been run, so nothing is known of what follows a first rise. This run is that loop in torch as the specification states it, under the envelope and the anchor: each length is the measured least point of the loss on the step's texts held fixed, the answers are then written again, and the loop goes on from there. It takes the derivative as it is, so that beside the balanced loop it shows what the tolerance and the refreshed trace do without any weighing of the update against the tokens inside their tolerance.
repeating_pattern_check: Four things have happened more than once. (1) A change fitted on one history read worse on the history the changed model has: the two whole-path sweeps raised the correct members' sum on the model's own answers from nothing, and the four gradient steps taken on a fixed text (plain, lattice, whitened, the rows through the parting) read 0.91 to 0.96 on that text and 1.2 to 3.7 times on the text torch then writes (records/development/2026-11-15-relation-reading/step-own-plain.json, step-own-lattice.json, step-own-whitened.json, step-own-plain-through.json). It keeps happening because the request was made on a history the changed model no longer has, and because correct paths were asked to move. Every derivative of this loop is taken on the own trace of the state it stands at, and nothing is asked of a pair inside the envelope. (2) An interim reading was taken for a verdict: the first rise on the own text was called damage, and Marcos corrected it (journal/2026-11-15-follow-the-changing-trace.md). This loop draws no verdict from a rise, a spike of the derivative or an answer's length; it records each step and goes on from the state it reached. (3) A surrogate's arithmetic was read as the model's computation: the torch forward stands a little off the engine, which at a near tie writes another token and at a tolerance's edge calls cells over it. The distances are anchored on the engine's here, and every reading of this run is named a trial in torch. (4) A sum hid where the loss sits: a shortened answer lays many original rows on one of its steps, and a loss cannot close on a stretch with no trace of its own. Each step keeps every answer's record of pairs and every original row's loss, mass and count of positions.
hypothesis: That the correction made again from each reached state on its own trace brings the wrong answers' computation toward the correct one although early steps may raise the own-trace loss: with nothing asked inside the successes' envelope, a state whose correct answers were moved has them over their tolerance, so the next derivative pulls them back while it goes on moving the wrong ones, and the own-trace loss comes back down from a first rise. It is a hypothesis about this construction in torch's arithmetic. It does not claim the mates are each answer's right destination (two members' mates are of another route), and a fall is no repair: closure is measured on the engine's own trace.
what_went_wrong_before: The first relational reference set its tolerance at the members' mean, which left a third of the loss, and of the gradient, on correct answers. The first steps were taken on the engine's recorded texts and judged on texts torch writes. An own-text rise after one step was reported as a finding against the update before any second step had been taken. In the preparation of this loop the torch forward alone, unanchored, put 0.156 of the gradient's gain on the fifteen correct answers under the envelope, where the engine's trace asks nothing of them (records/development/2026-11-15-relation-reading/grad-split-envelope.json); anchored, it read the engine's hinge on the original cell for cell in preparation (the objective 0.0526553 and 138,187 cells over, none of a correct answer); this run's first command makes the anchor again on its own card and records the same check.

rule.start: the original model's 70 matrices, held in float32 beside the model, which holds them rounded to BF16 as a file would
a_step: the model as it stands writes its thirty answers in torch (the vocabulary's first choice at each position until the ending token or the limit, both the recorder's)

each written answer is laid on the original's rows: one on one where its text is the original's own, as the capture registers identical inputs; by the computation otherwise (torch_forward.registered against the original's exported turns)
the loss is read at every pair and merge with the original rows' masses (the pairs of one original row share its mass), against the frozen envelope, the forward's distance anchored on the engine's
the derivative of that own-trace loss in the 70 matrices is taken through the whole path, both sides of every merge and attention differentiated
a length is searched along the direction (`length`)
the weights move by the length taken; the next step starts from there by writing the answers again, whatever was read
rule.direction: the derivative as it is: every matrix moves against its own part of the derivative of the loss on the step's own texts (direction=plain). Nothing weighs the update against the positions inside their tolerance; that is the balanced loop.
rule.length: on the step's own texts held fixed, by the anchored loss: the first length is the loss over the slope of the loss along the direction; a trial at h reading L(h) gives the parabola through the start's loss, the start's slope and L(h), whose least point is the next length; the search ends at the first trial that does not read under the lowest so far, once one has read under the start, and the step is the lowest (it also ends where the loss fell at least as fast as its straight line, with that trial as the step). Every trial is on BF16-rounded weights. This is a strict decrease of the surrogate on a history held fixed, as the specification states the rule; it cannot see an answer leave its text, and the own trace written again after the step is read whatever it says: no length is shortened and no step is undone by it.
rule.stall: a step whose search finds no length reading under its start, down to a length that moves no stored weight, ends the loop: the proposal has stalled, which is no closure
rule.closure: the loop ends when the own-trace loss is nothing (every pair inside its tolerance); in torch that is a trial's reading and no closure of the capability gap
rule.continuation: no state is kept or dropped by its loss, and no step is undone; no count of steps is set; a stop by hand (for the card, or on a direction) is recorded by a dated revision of this declaration with the steps then on file
rule.anchor: distance at a pair laid on original row r = (the engine's distance at r on the original) + (the forward's distance at the pair) - (the forward's distance at r on the original); made once by this run's first command from the original's weights on the original's own texts on this run's card, and held to its sha256
rule.kept_each_step: the own-trace loss by answer and by group, the cells over tolerance by group, the positions over it, the derivative's size and the share of its gain that comes from the answers that are not wrong, every trial with its length, reading and stored weights moved, and in loop/step-<n>.npz every answer's written tokens and record of pairs with each original row's loss by merge, mass and count of positions
rule.not_read: what any answer says; no token, word or value is a measure here, and an answer's length is recorded only as how its trace lies on the original's rows

prediction: The anchor's check repeats the preparation's: on the original's own texts the anchored forward reads the engine's objective (0.05266) with 138,187 cells over tolerance, none of a correct answer. In torch the own trace at the start is not the engine's for the answers that leave the recorded text at a near tie (9 of 30 in the earlier reading on card 1), so the loop's first own-trace loss stands above 0.0527 and some of it is on correct answers. The first step's length falls near the share of its unit the same rule took under the mean tolerance (2^-2.5); the weights then move by about 0.034 in all (the length times the derivative's size), against 0.105 for that step. Under the mean tolerance a move of 0.026 along the plain direction left 1 of 30 answers as written (records/development/2026-11-15-relation-reading/step-own-plain-along.json). So most answers are predicted to be rewritten by the first step and the own trace after it to read above its start. Of the continuation, which is what this run is for, the prediction is the weaker one: over the first ten steps most answers are rewritten at every step and the own-trace loss stays above its start, falling from its highest reading but not passing under the start. It is not predicted that the loss reaches nothing in the steps this run takes.
would_weaken_it: The own-trace loss still at or above its highest reading after ten steps (no coming back down from the first rise), or the correct answers' part growing step over step: the correction followed along the changing trace would then not be finding its way back in this form. The prediction, as distinct from the hypothesis, is wrong if the first step leaves most answers as written, or if the own trace passes under its start within ten steps; either would be the better news. A reading of the weights a step took that is not the next step's start reading on the same texts would mean the torch forward does not repeat itself, and the readings would not be exact.
limits: A trial in torch. The engine words answers differently from torch at near ties and differently on its two cards; nothing here is the measured loss, and the native loop is declared separately for admission.

The anchor carries the forward's difference from the engine at each original row to whatever position is laid on that row; away from the original's own texts that is an approximation of the surrogate, not a measurement.
Fitting answers only: the thirty of controlled-bf16-1. Nothing of the no-fit answers or the reserved set is read; of the cohort's capture and exports only the thirty fitting ids.

The mates and the envelope are the frozen bytes of relation-envelope-original and are not made again or adjusted from anything this run reads. Two members' mates are of another route; that limit stays.

A success sits exactly on the envelope wherever it is itself the widest witness (91,285 of the successes' 971,775 cells on the original), so after any step some of those cells stand over it by little and carry a full derivative: protection inside the same objective, counted each step.
The loops of this family run on different cards, each with its own anchor; their readings are compared as trajectories, not digit for digit.
No model file is written, no engine runs, and no closure, repair or verdict on the hypothesis follows from this run.

engine_distances.what: the engine's distance of every original row from each success at every merge; the mate's column is the engine's distance the anchor stands on

tolerance.derivation: Astra's envelope: at a row and a merge, the largest of the fifteen fitting successes' own distances from their mates carried to the row, the recipient's own included; loaded as frozen bytes and held to the sha256 bound above
tolerance.scales_with: the successes' own disagreement at that row and merge

anchor.derivation: the hinge of a pair is the part over zero of (the forward's distance at the pair - the forward's distance at its row on the original's weights and texts, made by this run's first command) + (the engine's distance at its row - the tolerance at its row)
anchor.scales_with: the torch forward's arithmetic on the card it runs on; made again for another card, model or reference

unit_length.derivation: each step: the loss the step starts from over the slope of the loss along the direction (the derivative's inner product with the direction)
unit_length.scales_with: the loss and its derivative at the state the step starts from

trial_lengths.derivation: the least points of parabolas through the readings, as `rule.length` states them; no factor, count or fraction is set
trial_lengths.scales_with: the readings of the loss along the direction

stored_format.derivation: the 70 matrices are held as the file holds them, BF16; what a step leaves under the rounding stays in the float32 copy for the next
stored_format.scales_with: the format a model file holds its weights in

writing.derivation: the recorder's limit of tokens and ending token, as that record holds them (`written.limit`, `written.ending_tokens`)

steps.derivation: no count: the loop ends at a loss of nothing or at a stall, and a stop by hand is recorded by a dated revision
